-- Modders: this editor uses public operations only. A scene keeps original
-- definition GUIDs, native classes, source paths and world poses. Temporary
-- entity/template handles stay in local variables and never enter game.state.
-- New projects are disabled. Use the launcher's Test action, open this page
-- through Options > Extras > Mods, then Save draft before closing the game.
local templates, template_index, template_page = {}, 1, 1
local definitions = {}
local template_indices = {}
local selected, undo, redo, pending = nil, {}, {}, nil
local message, step, turn_step, scale_step = "Load a level and choose a prop", 1, 15, 1.1
local ticks, saving, bound, last_message = 0, false, 0, nil
local page, refresh, begin_load
local MAX_OBJECTS, PAGE_SIZE = 64, 40

-- The original TV menu has single-row labels. Keep UTF-8 names readable
-- without wrapping into its next button; documents retain the full identity.
local function caption(text, limit)
    if utf8.len(text) <= limit then return text end
    return string.sub(text, 1, utf8.offset(text, limit - 2) - 1) .. "..."
end

local function copy(value)
    if type(value) ~= "table" then return value end
    local result = {}
    for k, v in pairs(value) do result[k] = copy(v) end
    return result
end
local function document() return game.state.scene end
local function object_index(id)
    for i, item in ipairs(document().objects) do if item.id == id then return i end end
end
local function item() local i = object_index(selected); return i and document().objects[i], i end
local function tagged(id) return game.world.tagged(id) end
local function same_source(a, b)
    return a.guid == b.guid and a.class == b.class
end
local function template_for(source)
    -- Reuse the current refresh, rather than converting hundreds of native
    -- catalog records to Lua again for every placement, duplicate and undo.
    -- These handles remain local and are rebuilt after loads and restores.
    return definitions[source.guid .. ":" .. source.class] or nil
end
local function fail(result)
    message = result.error or "The native operation could not finish"
    game.log.info((result.code or "scene") .. ": " .. message)
end
local function validate(value)
    local result = game.system.try_call("scenes.validate", {document = value})
    if not result.ok then fail(result); return end
    return result.value
end
local function history(before, after, index)
    undo[#undo + 1] = {before = copy(before), after = copy(after), index = index}
    if #undo > 64 then table.remove(undo, 1) end
    redo = {}
end
local function live_count()
    bound = 0
    if not game.world.status().ready then return end
    for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do if object_index(object.tag) then bound = bound + 1 end end
end
local function current_level()
    local world = game.world.status()
    if not world.ready or world.level_root == "" then
        message = "Wait for a level with a known episode catalog"
        return
    end
    if #document().objects > 0 and document().level_root ~= world.level_root then
        message = "This scene belongs to " .. document().level_root .. "; load it or start a new scene"
        return
    end
    return world
end
local function create(object)
    local template = template_for(object.source)
    if not template then return {ok = false, error = "Load the scene's original source before recreating this prop"} end
    local result = game.system.try_call("world.spawn", {template = template.id,
        position = object.transform.position, radius = object.radius, tag = object.id})
    if not result.ok then return result end
    local entity = result.value
    result = game.system.try_call("entities.set_transform", {entity = entity, transform = object.transform})
    if not result.ok then game.world.destroy(entity); return result end
    return {ok = true, value = entity}
end
local function next_id()
    repeat
        game.state.sequence = (game.state.sequence or 0) + 1
    until not object_index("scene-" .. game.state.sequence)
    return "scene-" .. game.state.sequence
end
local function record(template, position)
    return {id = next_id(), name = template.name, radius = 1,
        source = {guid = template.source_guid, class = template.class, stream = template.source_stream},
        transform = {position = position, right = {x = 1, y = 0, z = 0},
            up = {x = 0, y = 1, z = 0}, forward = {x = 0, y = 0, z = 1}}}
end
local function add(object)
    if #document().objects >= MAX_OBJECTS then message = "This scene already has 64 objects"; return end
    local world = current_level(); if not world then return end
    local candidate = copy(document()); candidate.level_root = world.level_root
    candidate.objects[#candidate.objects + 1] = copy(object)
    candidate = validate(candidate); if not candidate then return end
    local result = create(object)
    if not result.ok then fail(result); return end
    game.state.scene = candidate; selected = object.id
    history(nil, object, #candidate.objects)
    message = "Placed " .. object.name
    live_count()
end
local function edit(change)
    local object, index = item(); if not object then message = "Select a scene object first"; return end
    local entity = tagged(object.id); if not entity then message = "Load this scene's preview first"; return end
    local result = game.system.try_call("entities.transform", {entity = entity})
    if not result.ok then fail(result); return end
    local before, after = copy(object), copy(object)
    before.transform = result.value; after.transform = copy(result.value)
    change(after.transform)
    local candidate = copy(document()); candidate.objects[index] = after
    candidate = validate(candidate); if not candidate then return end
    result = game.system.try_call("entities.set_transform", {entity = entity, transform = after.transform})
    if not result.ok then fail(result); return end
    game.state.scene = candidate; history(before, after, index)
    message = "Updated " .. object.name
end
local function apply_history(entry, reverse)
    local target
    if reverse then target = entry.before else target = entry.after end
    local old
    if reverse then old = entry.after else old = entry.before end
    local id = (target or old).id
    local existing = tagged(id)
    if target and old then
        if not existing then message = "This object is no longer in the preview"; return false end
        local result = game.system.try_call("entities.set_transform", {entity = existing, transform = target.transform})
        if not result.ok then fail(result); return false end
    elseif target then
        if existing then message = "This scene object already exists"; return false end
        local result = create(target)
        if not result.ok then fail(result); return false end
    elseif existing then game.world.destroy(existing) end
    local index = object_index(id)
    if target then
        if index then document().objects[index] = copy(target)
        else table.insert(document().objects, math.min(entry.index, #document().objects + 1), copy(target)) end
        selected = id
    elseif index then
        table.remove(document().objects, index)
        selected = document().objects[math.min(index, #document().objects)]
        selected = selected and selected.id
    end
    live_count()
    return true
end
local function unload()
    if pending then
        game.assets.cancel_source()
        pending = nil
    end
    for _, value in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do if object_index(value.tag) then game.world.destroy(value.id) end end
    game.assets.release_source()
    templates, definitions = {}, {}
    bound, undo, redo = 0, {}, {}
    message = "Preview unloaded; the authored scene is kept"
end
local function rollback(reason)
    for _, id in ipairs(pending.created) do
        local entity = tagged(id)
        if entity then game.world.destroy(entity) end
    end
    game.assets.cancel_source()
    templates, definitions = {}, {}
    pending = nil
    live_count()
    if bound == 0 then game.assets.release_source() end
    message = reason
end
begin_load = function()
    local world = current_level(); if not world then return end
    if #document().objects == 0 then message = "This scene is empty"; return end
    pending = {index = 1, created = {}, requested = nil}
    undo, redo = {}, {}
    message = "Loading scene objects and native resources"
end
refresh = function()
    templates, definitions, template_indices = {}, {}, {}
    if game.world.status().ready then
        for _, value in ipairs(game.world.catalog()) do
            local key = value.source_guid .. ":" .. value.class
            if definitions[key] ~= nil then definitions[key] = false
            else definitions[key] = value end
            -- Start with placeable props. The factory is not proof of an NPC's
            -- encounter, navigation, collision or scripted-scene prerequisites.
            if value.category == "Props" and value.source_stream and value.source_stream ~= ""
                and value.source_guid and value.source_guid ~= string.rep("0", 32) then
                templates[#templates + 1] = value
                template_indices[value.id] = #templates
            end
        end
        live_count()
    else bound = 0 end
    template_index = math.max(1, math.min(template_index, #templates))
    template_page = math.floor((template_index - 1) / PAGE_SIZE) + 1
end
page = function()
    local doc = document(); if not doc then return end
    local choices, objects = {}, {}
    local first = (template_page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE + 1
    for index = first, math.min(#templates, first + PAGE_SIZE - 1) do
        -- Choices carry the exact current template identity. Desktop tools
        -- can select it without rebuilding the whole catalog on every place.
        -- These handles stay local; portable scene records still use GUIDs.
        choices[#choices + 1] = {label = index .. ": " .. caption(templates[index].name, 20), value = templates[index].id}
    end
    if #choices == 0 then choices = {{label = "Refresh loaded props", value = 0}} end
    for index, object in ipairs(doc.objects) do
        objects[#objects + 1] = {label = index .. ": " .. caption(object.name, 20), value = object.id}
    end
    if #objects == 0 then objects = {{label = "No authored objects", value = ""}} end
    if not object_index(selected) then selected = doc.objects[1] and doc.objects[1].id end
    local object = item()
    local rows = {
        {id = "summary", type = "text", label = #doc.objects .. "/64 authored; " .. bound .. " in preview"},
        {id = "level", type = "text", label = doc.level_root ~= "" and caption(doc.level_root, 32) or "Place a prop to choose an episode"},
        {id = "refresh", label = "Refresh loaded props"},
        {id = "template", type = "select", label = "Prop", value = templates[template_index] and templates[template_index].id or 0, choices = choices},
        {id = "previous-page", label = "Previous template page"},
        {id = "next-page", label = "Next template page"},
        {id = "place", label = "Place beside my character"},
        {id = "object", type = "select", label = "Object", value = selected or "", choices = objects},
        {id = "step", type = "select", label = "Movement step", value = step, choices = {
            {label = "0.1", value = 0.1}, {label = "1", value = 1}, {label = "5", value = 5}, {label = "10", value = 10}}},
        {id = "bring", label = "Bring selected object here"}
    }
    if object then
        for _, axis in ipairs({"x", "y", "z"}) do
            rows[#rows + 1] = {id = "position-" .. axis, type = "slider", label = "Position " .. string.upper(axis),
                value = object.transform.position[axis], min = -1000000, max = 1000000, step = step}
        end
    end
    for _, row in ipairs({
        {id = "turn-left", label = "Rotate left 15 degrees"}, {id = "turn-right", label = "Rotate right 15 degrees"},
        {id = "grow", label = "Grow by 10%"}, {id = "shrink", label = "Shrink by 10%"},
        {id = "duplicate", label = "Duplicate selected object"}, {id = "remove", label = "Remove selected object"},
        {id = "undo", label = "Undo (" .. #undo .. ")"}, {id = "redo", label = "Redo (" .. #redo .. ")"},
        {id = "load", label = "Load scene preview"}, {id = "cancel", label = "Cancel scene loading"},
        {id = "unload", label = "Unload preview"},
        {id = "autoload", type = "toggle", label = "Load automatically in this episode", value = doc.autoload},
        {id = "save", label = "Save scene draft"}, {id = "new", label = "Start a new empty scene"},
        {id = "status", type = "text", label = caption(message, 32)}
    }) do rows[#rows + 1] = row end
    if message ~= last_message then game.log.info(message); last_message = message end
    game.ui.register_page({id = "scene", title = "Scene editor", rows = rows})
end
local function initialize()
    if not game.state.scene then
        local project = game.scenes.document()
        game.state.scene = project.document
        local draft = game.storage.read("scene-draft.json")
        if draft and draft.fingerprint == project.fingerprint then game.state.scene = game.scenes.validate(draft.scene) end
    end
    game.state.scene = game.scenes.validate(game.state.scene)
    game.state.sequence = game.state.sequence or 0
    page()
end
game.on("initialize", initialize)
game.on("state.loaded", function()
    game.state.scene = game.scenes.validate(game.state.scene)
    undo, redo, pending = {}, {}, nil
    page()
end)
game.on("level.ready", function()
    refresh(); page()
    local world = game.world.status()
    if document().autoload and document().level_root == world.level_root and #document().objects > 0 then begin_load() end
end)
game.on("level.unloading", function()
    -- Guest teardown owns the old world. Never issue destruction with expired
    -- handles or start loading sources from an unloading callback.
    templates, definitions, template_indices, undo, redo, pending, bound = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, nil, 0
    message = "Scene kept; load its episode to preview it"
    page()
end)
local function rebound()
    -- Tags identify objects independently of temporary handles. Do not infer
    -- correspondence from list order or object counts after reload or restore.
    pending, undo, redo = nil, {}, {}
    refresh(); message = "Scene state restored; owned objects rebound by tag"; page()
end
game.on("code.reloaded", rebound)
game.on("save.restored", rebound)
game.on("entity.removed", function() live_count(); page() end)
game.on("frame", function()
    ticks = ticks + 1
    if saving and ticks % 15 == 0 then
        local status = game.storage.status()
        if status.pending == 0 then
            saving = false
            message = #status.errors == 0 and (game.state.mission_document
                and "Drafts saved; close Test, then Apply saved drafts"
                or "Draft saved; close Test, then Apply scene draft in the launcher") or "Draft write failed; check storage errors"
            page()
        end
    end
    if not pending then return end
    local object = document().objects[pending.index]
    if not object then pending = nil; refresh(); message = "Scene preview ready"; page(); return end
    if tagged(object.id) then pending.index = pending.index + 1; return end
    if pending.requested then
        local source = game.assets.source_status()
        if source.phase == "failed" then rollback(source.message); page(); return end
        if not source.ready then return end
        pending.requested = nil
        refresh()
        if not template_for(object.source) then rollback("The loaded archive has no matching definition and class"); page(); return end
    end
    if not template_for(object.source) then
        -- A first physics step can precede the final level IO completion.
        -- Keep the preview transaction intact while that work settles.
        if game.world.status().streaming then return end
        local result = game.system.try_call("assets.load_source", {stream = object.source.stream})
        if not result.ok and result.code == "busy" then return end
        if not result.ok then rollback(result.error); page(); return end
        pending.requested = object.source.stream
        message = "Loading " .. object.source.stream; page(); return
    end
    local result = create(object)
    if not result.ok then rollback(result.error); page(); return end
    pending.created[#pending.created + 1] = object.id
    pending.index = pending.index + 1
    live_count()
end)
game.on("ui.action", function(event)
    if event.page ~= "scene" then return end
    if event.row == "save" then
        -- A mission project shares this page. Save both documents in one
        -- storage replacement so neither editor can leave the other behind.
        local result
        if game.state.mission_document then
            result = game.system.try_call("projects.save_all", {documents = {scene = document(), mission = game.state.mission_document}})
            if result.ok then game.state.scene = result.value.scene end
        else
            result = game.system.try_call("scenes.save", {document = document()})
            if result.ok then game.state.scene = result.value end
        end
        if result.ok then saving = true; message = "Saving scene draft" else fail(result) end
        page(); return
    end
    if pending then
        if event.row == "cancel" then rollback("Scene load canceled; earlier preview objects are kept") end
        page(); return
    end
    if event.row == "step" then step = event.value; page(); return end
    if event.row == "object" then selected = event.value; page(); return end
    if event.row == "template" then
        local index = type(event.value) == "number" and event.value or template_indices[event.value]
        if index and templates[index] then template_index = index
        else message = "This template changed; refresh loaded props" end
        page(); return
    end
    if event.row == "autoload" then document().autoload = event.value; page(); return end
    if not game.world.status().ready then message = "Load a level first"; page(); return end
    if event.row == "refresh" then refresh()
    elseif event.row == "previous-page" or event.row == "next-page" then
        local pages = math.max(1, math.ceil(#templates / PAGE_SIZE))
        template_page = (template_page - 1 + (event.row == "next-page" and 1 or -1)) % pages + 1
        template_index = (template_page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE + 1
    elseif event.row == "unload" then unload()
    elseif event.row == "new" then
        unload(); game.state.scene = game.scenes.document().document
        game.state.scene.objects = {}; game.state.scene.level_root = ""; game.state.scene.autoload = false
        selected = nil; message = "New empty scene; Save draft replaces your previous draft"
    elseif not current_level() then page(); return
    elseif event.row == "load" then begin_load()
    elseif event.row == "place" then
        local actor, template = game.players.controlled(event.player), templates[template_index]
        if actor and template then
            local p = actor.position
            add(record(template, {x = p.x + 4, y = p.y + 1, z = p.z}))
        else message = "Choose a loaded prop and a controlled character" end
    elseif event.row == "duplicate" then
        local object = item()
        if object then
            local value = copy(object); value.id = next_id(); value.transform.position.x = value.transform.position.x + step
            add(value)
        end
    elseif event.row == "remove" then
        local object, index = item()
        if object then
            local entity = tagged(object.id); if entity then game.world.destroy(entity) end
            table.remove(document().objects, index); history(object, nil, index)
            selected = nil; message = "Removed " .. object.name; live_count()
        end
    elseif event.row == "undo" or event.row == "redo" then
        local source, target = event.row == "undo" and undo or redo, event.row == "undo" and redo or undo
        local entry = source[#source]
        if entry and apply_history(entry, event.row == "undo") then
            table.remove(source); target[#target + 1] = entry
            message = event.row == "undo" and "Edit undone" or "Edit reapplied"
        end
    elseif event.row == "bring" then
        local actor = game.players.controlled(event.player)
        if actor then edit(function(pose) local p = actor.position; pose.position = {x = p.x + 4, y = p.y + 1, z = p.z} end) end
    elseif string.sub(event.row, 1, 9) == "position-" then
        local axis = string.sub(event.row, 10)
        edit(function(pose) pose.position[axis] = event.value end)
    elseif event.row == "grow" or event.row == "shrink" or event.row == "turn-left" or event.row == "turn-right" then
        edit(function(pose)
            local angle = math.rad(event.row == "turn-left" and -turn_step or turn_step)
            local c, s = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
            for _, name in ipairs({"right", "up", "forward"}) do
                local v = pose[name]
                if event.row == "grow" or event.row == "shrink" then
                    local factor = event.row == "grow" and scale_step or 1 / scale_step
                    pose[name] = {x = v.x * factor, y = v.y * factor, z = v.z * factor}
                else pose[name] = {x = v.x * c + v.z * s, y = v.y, z = v.z * c - v.x * s} end
            end
        end)
    end
    page()
end)

-- Modders: this is an encounter authoring workshop, not a campaign replacement.
-- Choose a loaded NPCMelee template, including its original resources and
-- class callbacks. Author safe arena positions for your mission;
-- generic cloning alone does not establish every enemy's AI/script dependencies.
local mission_id, goal = "brawler-workshop", 2
local targets, sample_seconds = {}, 0
local templates, selected = {}, 1
local status = "Load a level and choose an NPC target template"

local function display_name(item)
    -- Keep the native menu readable even for a mod's long resource filename.
    if #item.name > 96 then return item.name:sub(1, 93) .. "..." end
    return item.name
end

local function template_key(item)
    -- Native resource GUIDs survive display-name changes and code reload.
    -- The name fallback keeps this example readable on older hosts; new
    -- projects should use model_resource when selecting a particular asset.
    if item.model_resource and item.model_resource ~= "" then return item.model_resource end
    return "name:" .. item.name
end

local function refresh_templates()
    templates = {}
    if not game.world.status().ready then selected = 1; return end
    for _, item in ipairs(game.world.catalog()) do
        if item.class == "NPCMelee" or
            (not item.class and item.category == "Enemies" and item.name == "Brawler") then
            templates[#templates + 1] = item
        end
    end
    selected = math.max(1, math.min(selected, #templates))
    for i, item in ipairs(templates) do
        if template_key(item) == game.state.template_resource then selected = i; break end
    end
end

local function page()
    local mission = game.missions.get(mission_id)
    local template = templates[selected]
    game.ui.register_page({id = "combat", title = "Combat workshop", rows = {
        {id = "state", type = "text", label = "Encounter: " .. mission.status},
        {id = "progress", type = "text", label = "Defeated: " .. mission.objectives[1].progress .. " / " .. goal},
        {id = "status", type = "text", label = status},
        {id = "template", type = "text", label = "Target: " .. (template and display_name(template) or "Load a level")},
        {id = "previous", label = "Previous loaded target template"},
        {id = "next", label = "Next loaded target template"},
        {id = "refresh", label = "Refresh loaded template names"},
        {id = "start", label = "Start beside my character"},
        {id = "retry", label = "Retry from the encounter checkpoint"},
        {id = "hit", label = "Apply a test hit (10 HP)"},
        {id = "heal", label = "Heal the remaining targets"},
        {id = "hide", label = "Hide my targets"},
        {id = "reveal", label = "Reveal my targets"},
        {id = "cancel", label = "End the encounter and remove my targets"}
    }})
end

local function cleanup()
    -- Mark our local set empty before requesting removal: removal is not a
    -- defeat, and the later entity.removed event must not complete objectives.
    targets = {}
    if not game.world.status().ready then return end
    for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do
        game.system.try_call("world.destroy", {entity = object.id})
    end
end

local function fail(reason)
    if game.missions.get(mission_id).status == "active" then
        game.missions.fail(mission_id, reason)
    end
    cleanup()
    status = reason
    page()
end

local function spawn_remaining(player)
    cleanup()
    local actor = game.players.controlled(player)
    if not actor then fail("Assign a player and load a playable level before retrying"); return end
    refresh_templates()
    local template
    for _, item in ipairs(templates) do
        if template_key(item) == game.state.encounter_template_resource then template = item; break end
    end
    if not template then
        fail("The encounter template is no longer loaded; choose a target and start again"); return
    end
    local mission = game.missions.get(mission_id)
    local remaining = goal - mission.objectives[1].progress
    local p = actor.position
    for i = 1, remaining do
        local spawned = game.system.try_call("world.spawn", {template = template.id,
            position = {x = p.x + 5, y = p.y + 0.25, z = p.z + (i - 1) * 3}, radius = 1})
        if not spawned.ok then fail("The native factory rejected this encounter template"); return end
        local health = game.system.try_call("entities.health", {entity = spawned.value})
        if not health.ok or not health.value or health.value.dead then
            fail("This template has no supported living health component"); return
        end
        targets[spawned.value] = true
    end
    status = display_name(template) .. ": use Test hit to inspect native damage; natural AI needs scene setup"
    page()
end

local function rebind()
    targets = {}
    refresh_templates()
    if not game.world.status().ready then page(); return end
    for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do targets[object.id] = true end
    -- Reload transfers objects; it must not spawn replacements. Exact saves
    -- rebind supported objects, while checkpoint loads create a fresh world.
    page()
end

game.on("initialize", function()
    game.missions.register({id = mission_id, title = "Brawler workshop", objectives = {
        {id = "defeat", title = "Defeat the encounter targets", goal = goal}
    }})
    game.state.elapsed, game.state.checkpoint_elapsed, game.state.player = 0, 0, 0
    game.state.template_resource, game.state.encounter_template_resource = "", ""
    page()
end)
game.on("state.loaded", page)
game.on("level.ready", rebind)
game.on("code.reloaded", rebind)
game.on("save.restored", function(event)
    if event.kind == "checkpoint" and game.missions.get(mission_id).status == "active" then
        game.missions.restart(mission_id)
        game.state.elapsed = game.state.checkpoint_elapsed or 0
        spawn_remaining(game.state.player or 0)
    else rebind() end
end)
game.on("level.unloading", function()
    targets, templates, selected = {}, {}, 1
    if game.missions.get(mission_id).status == "active" then
        game.missions.fail(mission_id, "The level changed; restart in the new playable area")
    end
    status = "Load a playable level before starting"
    page()
end)

game.on("ui.action", function(event)
    if event.page ~= "combat" then return end
    if event.row == "previous" or event.row == "next" or event.row == "refresh" then
        refresh_templates()
        if #templates > 0 then
            if event.row == "previous" then selected = (selected - 2) % #templates + 1 end
            if event.row == "next" then selected = selected % #templates + 1 end
            game.state.template_resource = template_key(templates[selected])
        end
        page()
    elseif event.row == "start" or event.row == "retry" then
        if not game.world.status().ready then status = "Load a level first"; page(); return end
        refresh_templates()
        if event.row == "start" then
            local template = templates[selected]
            if not template then status = "This level has no loaded NPCMelee target templates"; page(); return end
            game.state.template_resource = template_key(template)
            -- Browsing another template later must not replace this encounter's
            -- remaining targets during a retry or checkpoint restore.
            game.state.encounter_template_resource = template_key(template)
        end
        local mission = game.missions.get(mission_id)
        if event.row == "retry" and not mission.has_checkpoint then
            status = "Start the encounter to create its checkpoint"; page(); return
        end
        if mission.status == "idle" then game.missions.start(mission_id)
        else game.missions.restart(mission_id, event.row == "retry") end
        game.state.player = event.player -- The initiating logical P1/P2, not family-list order.
        game.state.elapsed = event.row == "retry" and (game.state.checkpoint_elapsed or 0) or 0
        if event.row == "start" then
            game.state.checkpoint_elapsed = 0
            game.missions.checkpoint(mission_id)
        end
        spawn_remaining(event.player)
    elseif event.row == "hit" then
        for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do
            if targets[object.id] then
                local hit = game.system.try_call("entities.damage", {entity = object.id, amount = 10})
                if not hit.ok then game.log.info(hit.code .. ": " .. hit.error) end
                break
            end
        end
    elseif event.row == "heal" then
        for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do
            if targets[object.id] then game.entities.heal(object.id, 1000000) end
        end
    elseif event.row == "hide" or event.row == "reveal" then
        -- Visibility is independent of AI, damage and collision. Repeated
        -- requests are safe: the host balances one hide request per object,
        -- preserves the game's other hide requests, and transfers it on reload.
        for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do
            if targets[object.id] then
                local result = game.system.try_call("entities.set_visible",
                    {entity = object.id, visible = event.row == "reveal"})
                if not result.ok then game.log.info(result.code .. ": " .. result.error) end
            end
        end
    elseif event.row == "cancel" then fail("Encounter ended by the player") end
end)

game.on("entity.died", function(event)
    if not targets[event.entity] then return end
    targets[event.entity] = nil
    local mission = game.missions.get(mission_id)
    if mission.status == "active" then
        -- Only the original native death signal advances this objective.
        -- Ordinary removal, streaming and world.destroy never count as kills.
        mission = game.missions.advance(mission_id, "defeat", 1)
        if mission.status == "active" then
            game.missions.checkpoint(mission_id)
            game.state.checkpoint_elapsed = game.state.elapsed
        else status = "Encounter complete" end
    end
    -- The class may already have deleted itself. An expired handle is an
    -- expected outcome, so retire any remaining body through a bounded call.
    game.system.try_call("world.destroy", {entity = event.entity})
    page()
end)
game.on("entity.removed", function(event)
    if not targets[event.entity] then return end
    targets[event.entity] = nil
    fail("A target left without a native defeat; retry the encounter")
end)
game.on("simulation", function(event)
    if game.missions.get(mission_id).status ~= "active" then return end
    game.state.elapsed = game.state.elapsed + event.seconds
    sample_seconds = sample_seconds + event.seconds
    if sample_seconds < 0.2 then return end
    sample_seconds = 0
    if game.state.elapsed >= 90 then fail("Time ran out; retry from the checkpoint"); return end
    local assigned, alive = false, false
    for player = 0, 1 do
        local actor = game.players.controlled(player)
        if actor then
            assigned = true
            local health = game.players.health(actor.id)
            alive = alive or not health or not health.dead
        end
    end
    if assigned and not alive then fail("Both active players are down; retry from the checkpoint") end
end)

-- Modders: this is a native camera authoring starter, not a screen overlay.
-- Open Options > Extras > Mods > Camera workshop. Fly the camera using its
-- normal controls, capture two views, then preview either without moving the
-- family. Positions use world coordinates with Y up; angles and the vertical
-- field of view use degrees. No guest addresses or renderer-specific code.
game.state.schema = 1
game.state.shots = {}
game.state.epoch = 0
game.state.freeze = false
game.state.status = "Load a level to begin"

local function page()
    -- Native menu rows have one line. Keep status text short; put detailed
    -- diagnostics in the mod log rather than wrapping over the next row.
    local mode = game.camera.status()
    game.ui.register_page({id = "camera", title = "Camera workshop", rows = {
        {id = "status", label = game.state.status, type = "text"},
        {id = "free", label = "Fly the camera", type = "toggle", value = mode.free},
        {id = "photo", label = "Freeze the scene", type = "toggle", value = mode.photo},
        {id = "capture_a", label = "Capture shot A"},
        {id = "preview_a", label = "Preview shot A"},
        {id = "capture_b", label = "Capture shot B"},
        {id = "preview_b", label = "Preview shot B"},
        {id = "wide", label = "Wide lens (80 degrees)"},
        {id = "normal", label = "Medium lens (60 degrees)"},
        {id = "close", label = "Close lens (35 degrees)"},
        {id = "release", label = "Finish and release my camera"}
    }})
end

local function refresh_world()
    local world = game.world.status()
    if world.ready and game.state.epoch ~= world.epoch then
        -- World-space captures belong to this particular scene. A checkpoint
        -- loads a fresh world; never silently apply an old scene's coordinates.
        -- Authored cinematic tracks need their own proven level dependencies.
        game.state.shots = {}
        game.state.epoch = world.epoch
        game.state.status = "Ready to capture a shot"
    end
    return world.ready
end

local function request(name, arguments)
    -- Expected host failures are recoverable. Lua errors and callback budgets
    -- still retire this mod; the kit then releases its camera automatically.
    local result = game.system.try_call(name, arguments or {})
    if not result.ok then
        game.log.info(result.error)
        game.state.status = "Camera request failed"
    end
    return result.ok
end

game.on("initialize", page)
game.on("level.ready", function() refresh_world(); page() end)
game.on("level.unloading", function()
    game.state.status = "Scene unloading"
    page()
end)
game.on("ui.action", function(event)
    if event.page ~= "camera" then return end
    if event.row == "release" then
        -- Release only the camera. This mod's other services, if you add any,
        -- stay active. Another mod's preceding camera request can resume.
        if request("camera.release") then game.state.status = "Camera released" end
    elseif not refresh_world() then
        game.state.status = "Load a level first"
    elseif event.row == "free" then
        if request("camera.free", {enabled = event.value}) then
            game.state.status = "Fly, then capture a shot"
        end
    elseif event.row == "photo" then
        if request("camera.photo", {enabled = event.value}) then
            game.state.freeze = event.value
            game.state.status = event.value and "Scene frozen" or "Scene running"
        end
    elseif event.row == "capture_a" or event.row == "capture_b" then
        local pose = game.camera.pose()
        if pose then
            local slot = event.row == "capture_a" and "a" or "b"
            -- Store values in game.state, not a local reference to that table.
            -- Code reload restores the table and keeps these shots in this world.
            game.state.shots[slot] = pose
            game.state.status = "Captured shot " .. string.upper(slot)
        else game.state.status = "Camera not ready" end
    elseif event.row == "preview_a" or event.row == "preview_b" then
        local slot = event.row == "preview_a" and "a" or "b"
        local pose = game.state.shots[slot]
        if not pose then game.state.status = "Capture shot " .. string.upper(slot) .. " first"
        elseif request("camera.set_pose", {pose = pose}) then
            request("camera.photo", {enabled = game.state.freeze})
            game.state.status = "Previewing shot " .. string.upper(slot) .. ""
        end
    elseif event.row == "wide" or event.row == "normal" or event.row == "close" then
        local pose = game.camera.pose()
        if pose then
            pose.fov_degrees = event.row == "wide" and 80 or (event.row == "close" and 35 or 60)
            if request("camera.set_pose", {pose = pose}) then
                game.state.status = "Lens changed"
            end
        else game.state.status = "Camera not ready" end
    end
    page()
end)

local function finite(value, low, high)
    return type(value) == "number" and value == value and value >= low and value <= high
end
local function valid_pose(pose)
    if type(pose) ~= "table" or type(pose.position) ~= "table" or type(pose.rotation) ~= "table" then
        return false
    end
    for _, axis in ipairs({"x", "y", "z"}) do
        if not finite(pose.position[axis], -1000000, 1000000) then return false end
    end
    return finite(pose.rotation.pitch, -90, 90) and finite(pose.rotation.yaw, -180, 180)
        and finite(pose.rotation.roll, -180, 180) and finite(pose.fov_degrees, 1, 120)
end
game.on("state.loaded", function()
    -- Validate saved values before a code reload commits. This callback must
    -- not apply a pose: gameplay writes are forbidden during restore preflight.
    if game.state.schema ~= 1 or type(game.state.shots) ~= "table"
        or not finite(game.state.epoch, 0, 9007199254740991)
        or game.state.epoch % 1 ~= 0 or type(game.state.freeze) ~= "boolean"
        or type(game.state.status) ~= "string" or #game.state.status > 1024 then
        error("Camera workshop state needs migration")
    end
    for slot, pose in pairs(game.state.shots) do
        if (slot ~= "a" and slot ~= "b") or not valid_pose(pose) then
            error("Camera workshop shot needs migration")
        end
    end
    game.state.status = "Shots restored"
    page()
end)
game.on("code.reloaded", page)
game.on("save.restored", function() refresh_world(); page() end)

operations.name: scenes.document
operations.description: Read this mod package's validated scene and frozen source fingerprint without filesystem access. An absent scene returns an empty authoring document. Scene objects use original definition GUIDs, stream paths, stable per-owner tags and world poses, never temporary handles.

operations.name: scenes.validate
operations.description: Validate and canonicalize a portable scene document. Enforces unique tags, an unambiguous episode root, original GUID/class/source identities, bounded nonsingular float32 poses, radius limits and at most 64 objects. Does not spawn or change storage.

operations.name: scenes.save
operations.description: Queue this mod's validated scene draft in persistent storage, with its frozen source fingerprint. Check storage.status for completion. The launcher's Apply scene draft action copies a matching creator-Test draft into the editable package before export. This does not write code or replace game files.

operations.name: world.tagged
operations.description: Find this generation's live owned object by its stable tag. Returns a fresh entity handle or nil; pending removals are excluded. Tags survive supported code reload and exact restore. This capability identifies builds that support tagged world.spawn.

operations.name: timers.schedule
operations.description: Schedule or replace this mod's simulation timer. Pauses and menu redraws do not advance it. A timer event carries id, data and skipped intervals; repeats coalesce after a slow frame instead of catching up in a loop. Timers are saved with mod state.

operations.name: timers.cancel
operations.description: Cancel a timer owned by this mod. Returns whether it was pending.

operations.name: timers.list
operations.description: List this mod's pending timers, remaining simulation seconds, repeat intervals and event data.

operations.name: text.lookup
operations.description: Read a loaded game text ID as UTF-8, including active native language packs. IDs are listed by the translation exporter; unloaded entries report found=false.

operations.name: assets.search
operations.description: Search the game-wide resource library by category, name or a 32-digit native resource_id. Locations include native resource GUIDs when the named header provides one. Indexing is asynchronous; asset identities are not loaded entity templates.
operations.returns: index progress, categories and a bounded page of named resources

operations.name: assets.templates
operations.description: List original object definitions using an indexed asset, including native model/character references and source stream paths. Friendly names are available before loading. A supported definition becomes a resident_template after its source is ready; pass that current handle to world.spawn. Geometry references can have several original object variants.
operations.returns: ready, total and paged source object records

operations.name: assets.load_source
operations.description: Asynchronously add a source archive and its original native dependencies to a shared retained session. Up to eight archives can coexist; additions are serialized and a failed addition rolls back without removing earlier objects or resources. Each generation leases the whole session, with its latest requested root reported by source_status. Poll readiness, then reacquire a resident handle from assets.templates or world.catalog. Source actors stay inactive. Require assets.source_streams for multi-source capability on older builds.

operations.name: assets.source_status
operations.description: Report this generation's selected source, readiness and request errors. Existing sources stay ready while another owner adds an archive. streams lists every committed archive; pending_stream names the current addition. Native progress counts the shared session. A failed addition restores preceding leases and reports failure only to its waiting owners.

operations.name: assets.source_streams
operations.description: List committed archive paths in the shared native source session. This capability identifies builds that support combining sources. Shared dependencies remain resident until the last session owner releases; individual archives are not independently unloaded.

operations.name: assets.cancel_source
operations.description: Withdraw only this generation's pending addition and restore its preceding lease, including one acquired by a successful spawn from an old source. Existing objects and archives stay loaded. Native rollback starts when every waiting owner withdraws. Does not release a committed session; use release_source for that.

operations.name: assets.release_source
operations.description: Release this generation's whole source-session lease. Original native retirement runs after the last owner releases, removing the session's objects and archives together. Other owners keep all retained resources. Failed additions expire only their own temporary data. Reload and exact saves retain committed roots and claims; checkpoint/world changes discard them.

operations.name: locale.current
operations.description: Return the active mod language code, such as en or pt-br.

operations.name: locale.text
operations.description: Look up this mod's localized text with regional and source-language fallback; substitute named {values}. Button tags remain dynamic.

operations.name: system.describe
operations.description: Describe every implemented operation and its arguments.

operations.name: mods.status
operations.description: List loaded mods, creator credits, errors and callback costs.

operations.name: system.try_call
operations.description: Invoke one named host API with a named-argument object and return {ok=true,value=...} or {ok=false,code=...,error=...} for an expected host failure. Target validation, ownership, save read-only and preflight restrictions still apply. Cannot wrap itself or run a Lua function; interpreter errors and callback limits remain fatal. Use this for expected spawn or transform rejection, rather than pcall (which the sandbox disables).

operations.name: log.info
operations.description: Write a message attributed to this mod in the game log.

operations.name: storage.read
operations.description: Read this mod's cached persistent JSON; missing files return nil. Storage is loaded before callbacks start.

operations.name: storage.write
operations.description: Queue an atomic JSON write to this mod's persistent storage without blocking the game thread. Reads see the queued value immediately; use storage.status to check completion and errors.

operations.name: storage.status
operations.description: Report this mod's pending persistent writes and disk errors. Pending zero with no errors means all writes have reached the filesystem.

operations.name: world.status
operations.description: Get the current level readiness, location and world epoch. level_root is the unique loaded episode catalog excluding retained foreign sources; empty means it cannot be proven, so portable scenes must wait. streaming reports unfinished native file/manager work; scene autoload waits for it before requesting additional sources.

operations.name: players.list
operations.description: List the loaded family, including AI actors, with temporary handles, character names, positions, health and input_player. A slot is a family-list index; input_player is logical port 0/1 or null for AI, unbound or ambiguous ownership.

operations.name: players.controlled
operations.description: Get the family character currently bound to logical input player 0 or 1, or nil when no level/actor is ready or ownership is ambiguous. Requery during simulation after character switches, co-op joins, dropouts and restores; a previous actor handle may still identify a live AI character. This reads the game binding without polling devices. Paused or temporarily blocked controls do not change the binding.

operations.name: players.teleport
operations.description: Move one loaded player using the game's two world transforms.

operations.name: players.refill_health

operations.name: entities.move

Does not sweep for collision clearance or stop an authored controller from moving it afterward.

Includes orientation, scale, cached native scale and model/controller notifications. Converts the whole matrix through rotated, scaled or sheared parents. Nonfinite, singular or native-length overflow/underflow bases reject before dispatch; invalid frames or unavailable setters fail without a raw-write fallback. # Asset previews and format support

Open **Assets → Whole game** to browse the installed files without starting
Play. The background index uses the same native resource reader as the runtime.
It reports progress, keeps the original archives in place and includes the
current project's file replacements. Inspector shows resource GUIDs, source
locations and types.

Pause over a model row for a rotating 3D hover card. **3D preview** opens a
larger view: drag left to orbit, drag right or middle to pan, use the wheel to
zoom, and press **F** to frame the geometry. Spin can be turned off. Moving
between rows delays decoding briefly; a bounded cache reuses recently viewed
geometry and checks its source timestamps. Hidden previews stop animating.

These views draw the real decoded vertices and triangles. They show geometry
in its bind pose with neutral inspection lighting. Native materials, animation,
effects and behavior are checked in the map/Play renderer. A model's first
declared render part supplies its geometry preview; collision references stay
separate. Types or vertex declarations without a reviewed reader show their
specific limitation instead of a substitute model.

## Put a library object in a map

1. Open a Scene or Mission project and choose **Load level** above the viewport.
   The editor loads the original map and pauses its camera with fresh private
   progress. Your normal playthrough is separate.
2. Drag an object from the whole-game library onto the map viewport. Choose its
   original definition when the model has several variants.
3. The native source loader retains the archive and dependencies, reports
   progress and supports cancellation. Placement then uses the existing Scene
   operations and undo history. Current qualified Scene placement is for props;
   other factories report their unsupported behavior rather than guessing.
4. Use Inspector for position, rotation, scale, duplication and removal. Save
   live drafts, stop the workspace and apply the saved drafts to keep the mod.

**Native prop preview** is temporary: it frames an owned prop in the loaded map
and hides supported neighboring actors. **Clear preview** removes only that
temporary instance. It is never silently added to the Scene document.

## Extend a missing type

Use the named format layers instead of patching generated game functions:

- `modkit/src/streams.cpp` identifies resource types and reports GUIDs, source
  locations, references and object definitions. Keep unknown bytes intact.
- Typed readers such as `models.cpp`, `meshes.cpp` and `textures.cpp` describe
  original resources. Add a reader beside them for a new format, with explicit
  capability/reason fields for unsupported layouts.
- `modkit/src/stream_tool.cpp` exposes standalone inspection/export commands.
  The desktop `AssetStore` dispatches readers, checks exact identities and
  decodes off the UI thread. `MeshView` consumes real geometry buffers.
- A writer must validate the source fingerprint, identity, counts, bounds and
  untouched fields before producing a compact mod. Preserve topology until a
  new import path has its own native loader and collision qualification.
- Gameplay support belongs in a named operation in `modkit/api.json` with its
  adapter in `simpsons/src/modkit_game.cpp`. Reuse owned handles, source retention
  and normal teardown. Extend commented templates and regenerate the API help
  and completion when adding an operation.

Start with an inspect-only reader and a real original resource. Prove unchanged
round trips and malformed-input rejection before enabling edits. Then qualify
native load, save/reload and retirement. Source/type fixtures can cover large
inventories without playing through the campaign; behavior needs representative
native execution. Mesh, model, texture, scene and ownership fixtures provide
concrete examples.

Full offline map authoring, textured/animated previews, native studio backgrounds,
camera-correct placement and transform gizmos remain in
[the editor plan](EDITOR_PLAN.md). A geometry hover card does not qualify those
separate workflows.

# Native camera authoring

Choose **Camera workshop** in the desktop Modkit application, or run:

```sh
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py new "My camera shots" --template camera-workshop --id yourname.camera --author "Your name"
```

Creation leaves the project disabled. Its commented source adds a page in
**Options > Extras > Mods**. Fly the camera, capture shots A and B, preview
either shot, freeze the scene, change the lens, then release the camera.
The page uses the original Options movie. Captures survive code reload in the
same world; a new scene instance clears them. The starter deliberately avoids
applying coordinates from a previous checkpoint or level.

## Pose and lens

`game.camera.pose()` returns the last applied viewport 0 pose, or `nil` when no
supported level view is available. Positions are world coordinates with Y up.
Rotation contains pitch, yaw and roll in degrees. Yaw zero looks toward +Z;
positive yaw turns toward +X. Positive pitch looks down.

```lua
game.on("ui.action", function(event)
    if event.page ~= "my-page" then return end
    local pose = game.camera.pose()
    if event.row == "closer-lens" and pose then
        pose.fov_degrees = 35
        game.camera.set_pose(pose)
    elseif event.row == "finish" then
        game.camera.release()
    end
end)
```

`game.camera.set_pose(pose)` accepts a complete pose and returns its canonical
requested value. Each position axis is finite and within ±1,000,000. Pitch is
−90 through 90 degrees. Yaw and roll accept ±360,000 degrees and normalize to
−180 through 180. `fov_degrees` is the **actual vertical angle**, from 1 through
120 degrees. Unknown fields and invalid values reject before the working
request changes. Use `system.try_call` for expected host failures.

The game applies a pose on its next native camera update. Reading immediately
after a request can still return the preceding applied view. The original
camera writer updates the RenderWare frame and projection. Its different
director/aspect conventions are accounted for using the actual view window;
a wider screen keeps the requested vertical lens angle.

## Ownership and manual controls

Setting a pose enables the free camera and keeps the current photo-mode value.
Use `camera.photo(true)` to freeze the scene or `camera.photo(false)` to let
simulation run. Photo mode pauses simulation timers as well as characters and
physics. It is useful for staging; it is not a real-time cinematic clock.

The latest active camera request wins. `camera.release()` releases only the
calling mod generation's camera. Another mod's preceding explicit pose can
resume; the last release restores the captured manual camera or gameplay
modes. Other owned services stay active. Repeated release is safe, and mod
failure or retirement releases the camera automatically.

Manual camera movement, looking, zooming, reset or mode controls supersede old
mod requests. Retiring an old request then leaves the player's manual view
alone. Capturing a shot reads values and does not acquire a camera lease.

Camera poses contain no guest pointers or entity handles. Resource snapshots
retain request order, poses and the prior manual baseline. Legacy mode-only
snapshots remain supported. Checkpoints discard old-world camera requests;
exact/reload preflight validates them before replacing the running instance.
Full-scene exact restore, cinematic tracks and visual track editing remain
part of the [full gate](PLAN.md).

This API authors viewport 0. Either logical player can operate the native
workshop page, but this is not separate camera-track control for both co-op
viewports. Native Windows and Pixel behavior require their own qualification.

# Find and extend a game system

The generated C++ already executes natively. Its register operations and address-based
names come from mechanical PowerPC translation. A descriptive name helps navigation;
it does not recover an original class layout, function signature or source implementation.
The modkit's named APIs supply the usable interface for modders.

## Search without running the game

From the source checkout:

```sh
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py code build
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py code status
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py code search health
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py code show ScoreKeeper.GetScore
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py code callers ScoreKeeper.GetScore
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py code callees sub_828A31A8
```

The same index is used by `tools/codegraph/recomp_index.py`. To keep it elsewhere,
put `--db /path/to/code.sqlite` immediately after `code` on each command. Building
with `--source /path/to/checkout` selects another source tree. Queries return JSON
for use in editors and creator scripts. `--limit` bounds a result page; `more`
reports truncation.

`show` accepts a readable name, a `sub_XXXXXXXX` symbol or an exact hexadecimal entry
address. It returns the definition's path and lines, a body hash, indirect-call count,
source references and any reviewed alias. Aliases include their evidence and related
public API names. References cover the hand-written game adapters and research notes.
They help explain the code; the catalog does not claim those notes prove every use.

The index distinguishes direct and original-implementation calls, keeps recursion,
and records each call site's line. Comments and diagnostic string literals are excluded.
Indirect calls are counted separately: function pointers, vtables and runtime dispatch
need additional analysis. An empty direct-caller list does not mean a function is unused.
`gap` shows neighboring starts; it cannot establish function extents.

The registration audit compares address functions with the generated entrypoint table.
Named runtime imports and compiler helpers are counted separately. Missing definitions,
unmapped definitions and mismatched addresses are explicit. These are code-navigation
checks, not proof of campaign correctness or renderer coverage.

## Keep results current

Inputs include generated sources, game adapters, research notes, the API catalog,
the readable-name registry and the indexer itself. SHA-256 inventories detect changed
contents, added files and deleted files, including edits that preserve a timestamp.
Queries refuse stale results. Run `code build` again after editing those inputs.
An unchanged build reuses the database.

Rebuilding uses a private temporary database and checks the inputs again before replacing
the old one. A failed or interrupted build preserves the previous index. The index is
reproducible and does not belong in a mod package. Building and querying do not create
a mod profile or touch saves.

## Add a readable name

`symbols.json` stores reviewed descriptive names. Each entry supplies:

- The stable address symbol and an unambiguous readable name.
- The game system and a concrete description of the behavior.
- The reviewed definition hash from `code show`.
- Source-relative evidence paths with exact quoted passages.
- Related implemented operation names from `api.json`, when available.

Use descriptions such as `ScoreKeeper.GetScore` to make research searchable. Preserve
the original symbol in generated code, hook declarations and dispatch tables. Do not
automatically copy a caller's name onto its callees or infer a class from neighboring
addresses. Library matches, strings, script registrations and vtables can provide leads;
verify their relationship before publishing a descriptive name or typed adapter.

The tool rejects duplicate names, missing definitions, unknown API links and evidence
paths outside the checkout. If a definition or quoted passage changes, the rebuilt entry
is marked `needs_review`. Review the implementation and callers before updating its hash
or evidence. A matching hash means the reviewed text is unchanged; it is not an independent
verification of the behavior.

The initial registry covers progression, menus, entities, player damage, characters,
resources, text, input, simulation and rendering. Unnamed functions remain discoverable
by address, direct calls and source references. They have not all been reconstructed into
high-level source.

## Turn research into a mod API

Start with `api.json` and the generated reference. Extend an existing operation when its
contract fits; avoid creating a second interface for the same behavior.

For a new system, establish argument and return types, valid thread/context, ownership,
initialization and cleanup from the implementation and callers. Add the game-thread adapter,
then expose it through the shared Lua/C++ catalog. Handles must expire on deletion, unload
and restore. Reversible host changes need per-mod ownership and retirement. Persistent
changes need checkpoint, exact-save, code-reload and error behavior.

Generate the completion and reference together:

```sh
python3 tools/modkit/generate_api.py --output modkit/generated
```

Qualify a creator project against that contract before describing the feature as supported.
This keeps the address-level investigation inside the adapters so modders can work with
players, missions, cameras and assets through named operations.

# Health and combat authoring

Use the original health system through named operations. These APIs execute on
the game thread and share the usual mod ownership, callback and save guards.

| Target | Read | Scripted hit | Healing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Loaded family member | `game.players.health(id)` | `game.players.damage(id, amount)` | `game.players.heal(id, amount)` |
| This mod's owned object | `game.entities.health(id)` | `game.entities.damage(id, amount)` | `game.entities.heal(id, amount)` |

Read returns `{current, maximum, dead, enabled}`, or nil when the object has no
recognized health component. The healing limit comes from that component. The
legacy `players.list().max_health` field is the game's separate low-health
reference, which can differ. A generic entity getter returning 1 does not prove
that a prop has health.

Damage and healing accept finite amounts from 0 to 1,000,000. Their reply is
`{before, after, removed}`. Zero is a no-op. Native protection, damage masks,
character cooldowns and class filters can leave health unchanged. `enabled`
describes the component flag; it does not promise that every hit will count.
`dead` uses the game's death predicate, including its immortal-at-zero policy.
Healing respects the native limit and does not resurrect dead actors.

Scripted damage has no attacker or faction attribution. The host creates the
game's original damage record with its current simulation timestamp and the
target's resolved world impact position. It then runs the original entity dispatcher,
including subscriber activation and all listening components, followed by native
eligibility, hit, recovery and death handling. A target needs a supported world
transform for damage. The host never subtracts hit points directly, fabricates
an attacker or clears cooldown/protection flags. `players.refill_health` and
the debug menu's refill now use native healing too.

Native callbacks may remove an object. `removed` identifies a lifetime ending
during the request; `after` is nil if that happened or the health component is
no longer available. Do not assume disappearance establishes a kill, or keep
using a handle without checking its lifetime. Owned operations reject another
mod, another runtime generation and objects queued for removal. Stock objects
cannot be damaged through an owned handle.

```lua
local actor = game.players.controlled(0)
if actor then
    local health = game.players.health(actor.id)
    if health and not health.dead then game.players.heal(actor.id, 10) end
end
for _, object in ipairs(game.world.owned()) do
    local health = game.entities.health(object.id)
    if health and not health.dead then
        local result = game.system.try_call("entities.damage", {entity = object.id, amount = 10})
        if not result.ok then game.log.info(result.code .. ": " .. result.error) end
        break
    end
end
```

C++ plugins have typed `Health` and `HealthChange` records through
`PlayerHealth`, `EntityHealth`, `DamagePlayer`, `DamageEntity`, `HealPlayer` and
`HealEntity`. An absent component becomes `std::nullopt`. The Lua completion
and generated API reference describe the same replies.

## Native deaths and encounter progress

`entity.died` comes from the original health death handler, once per owned
object lifetime. It contains `entity`, which may already be stale. Native hooks
queue the notice; the host delivers it to the owning runtime after the current
callback returns, before removal notices. It does not reenter Lua from a hit.
World teardown uses `level.unloading` instead.

`entity.removed` also covers streaming, explicit removal and ordinary cleanup.
It is not a defeat event. Calling `world.destroy` never awards a native death.
An encounter should advance an objective on `entity.died`, then treat a target
leaving without that event as a separate authored condition.

Queued and delivered death states are recorded in host ownership. Code reload
transfers those states; an already reported death does not count twice. The
game adapter finishes queued combat notifications before applying a reload.
A save requested while notices remain queued reports `busy`; try again after
the next frame. This prevents freezing mission progress before its native death
notification while omitting a target already queued for cleanup.

## Combat workshop

Choose **Combat workshop** in the desktop Modkit application, or run:

```sh
python3 tools/modkit/modkit.py new "My encounter" --template combat-workshop --id yourname.encounter --author "Your name"
```

Creation leaves the project disabled. The commented source adds an original
Options page with a loaded NPC template picker, two owned targets, a defeat objective, native test
hits/healing, hide/reveal actions, a simulation deadline, failure and checkpoint retry. Either
logical player can start it beside their own character. Retry creates only
the remaining targets; code reload rebinds existing objects without duplicates.
Natural deaths and the test-hit action use the same native death event.
The [visibility operations](ENTITIES.md#visibility-and-encounter-setup) preserve
native hide requests across reload; hiding a target does not pause its AI or
make it harmless.

Use **Previous/Next loaded target template** to choose an NPCMelee variant.
Native model GUIDs distinguish templates with equal display labels. Names come
from the original resource loader where available; opening the asset library
can supply additional source metadata asynchronously. **Refresh loaded template
names** updates the picker afterwards. Browsing another model does not
change a running encounter's checkpoint. Retry finds the original model using
a fresh template handle, and fails cleanly if it is no longer loaded instead of
silently substituting another NPC. A missing supported health component also
rolls back the partial encounter.
Author arena positions and qualify enemy AI, collision and script dependencies
for the level you distribute. The generic factory does not establish those
properties for every enemy. This is an encounter authoring workshop; campaign
mission HUD integration, ability/targeting APIs, broader enemy classes and the
visual encounter editor remain in the [full plan](PLAN.md).

The private GAME_HUB staging scene exposed different model resources collapsed
under the old `Brawler` label: Frink and four 8-bit family variants. Native GUIDs
now match their original archive metadata and remain separate catalog entries.
Controlled close views now show the source Frink and its copy alike, with the
same 26 native geometry/material bindings across two LODs, also unchanged after
a simulation update. The earlier appearance-mismatch diagnosis came from
misleading rear views and family occlusion. Original scripts can still configure
more than a factory record supplies. This qualifies the inspected Frink copy;
broader classes, scripted appearances and natural combat AI remain in the gate.

The isolated checks execute the actual workshop source for co-op initiation,
native-event routing, ordinary removal, checkpoint retry, reload, completion,
timeout and failed spawning. The native health fixture executes unchanged game
routines, including the character cooldown filter and intrusive references.
Private Linux scene runs qualify actual resources separately. Windows/ARM64
compilation and Windows fixtures through Proton do not establish native Windows
driver behavior or Pixel device qualification.

# Make a mod with the desktop editor

The separate Windows/Linux **Modkit** application has **File → New project**. It uses
the same project format, commented scripts and package validation as the creator CLI.
A current game build with Modkit support is required for Test.

## Create and edit

1. Open **File → New project**. Choose **Gameplay tools**, **There and back**,
   **Mission editor**, **Input observer**, **Owned objects**, **Library objects**, **Combat workshop**,
   **Camera workshop**, **Scene editor**, or **File replacements**.
2. Enter a name, a stable id such as yourname.my-route, your creator credit and a
   description. The id identifies saved mod progress; keep it when updating the same mod.
3. Create the project. It starts disabled and does not change the installed mod profile.
4. Use **Project files** to open the commented Lua, language catalog, README or mod.json.
   **Save source** writes your edits. The editor refuses to overwrite a file that
   another editor changed after you opened it; reopen that file before continuing.

Gameplay tools adds a page in the original Options movie with health, protection and
camera controls. There and back is an authored route with dependent objectives, a time
limit, failure, an objective retry point and saved progress. Read the [mission guide](MISSIONS.md)
before changing its rules. File replacements starts with an empty gamedata folder.
Copy only the edited resources your mod needs, using paths matching your own installed game.
The [asset tools](README.md#asset-library) cover container inspection and rebuilding.

**Mission editor** authors reach, continuous stay and wait objectives in the native
menu, alongside the shared prop Scene editor. Save both drafts, close Test, then
choose **Apply saved drafts**. **Mission settings** offers a guided form for
titles, rules and prerequisites; **Edit JSON** opens the same source document.
Read the [editor guide](MISSION_EDITOR.md) for retry, pause and package behavior.

Camera workshop captures and previews native camera poses, changes lenses and releases
only its camera request. It uses the original Options menu and keeps captures through
code reload in the same scene. Read the [camera guide](CAMERAS.md) for coordinate,
ownership, lens and checkpoint rules.

**Scene editor** authors a prop scene through the game's Options menu: position,
rotation, scale, duplication and undo/redo. Use **Save scene draft**, wait for
confirmation and close Test. **Apply scene draft** copies that test's validated
document into mod.json for review and export, preserving your creator credit.
A draft made before source changes is rejected; re-test the new source first.
See [scene authoring](SCENES.md) for original-resource identity, autoload and limits.

The source editor supports existing UTF-8 Lua, JSON, Markdown, text, configuration and
XML files up to 128 KiB. Character, map, mission and cinematic editors remain
in development. Desktop projects can also be opened in an external
editor at the displayed folder. Lua projects include local completion definitions for
the named game APIs.

## Validate and test

**Validate** checks the package's metadata, files, checksums, dependencies and load order.
It reports overlapping file replacements. This does not prove Lua behavior, resource
compatibility or game correctness; use **Test** for that.

**Test** starts the project and its declared dependencies with a private profile and a
separate progress folder. Other selected mods and normal progress stay intact. The first
test starts with fresh progress. Later tests of the same id retain that test progress.
For scripted route projects, enter a playable level and use **Options → Extras → Mods**
to start the route. Testing does not automatically complete the campaign or start a mission.

Close the game before using the launcher source editor again. Code reload during play is
also available through the [creator bridge](README.md#timers-and-creator-inspection);
changing file replacements or translations needs a restart. A failed code replacement
keeps the running instance.

Native mod pages refresh when background work changes their rows or titles.
Editing a value keeps that control selected; a page that becomes shorter
returns to a valid page. Unchanged pages keep their native animations running.

Generated projects declare the operations and events their templates use. The native
validator checks these requirements before loading callbacks. Desktop Test also checks
the selected build's capability descriptor, so an older runtime produces an update
message rather than trying to run unsupported mission APIs.

The manifest fields requires_operations and requires_events are arrays of public API
names. Keep them up to date when adding a new operation or handler to your project.
They describe requirements, not permission to call APIs outside registered callbacks.

## Export and install

Save your edits, update the version and description in mod.json, then choose **Export ZIP**.
Desktop writes the package to the mods folder's exports directory and shows its location.
Android opens the document picker so you can save directly to Downloads or another provider.
The package contains public source and creator credit, with a checksummed inventory.
Local editor metadata and completion caches stay outside the package.

Another player installs that ZIP through **Mods → Install mod from ZIP**. It stays disabled
until they choose Enable. They see the creator, version and description; dependencies are
resolved before play. Share your own changes and required resources. Do not redistribute
default.xex, an extracted game, or unmodified game archives.

## Development checks

Regenerate the launcher bundle after changing either template or the generated Lua reference:

    python3 tools/modkit/generate_templates.py
    python3 tools/modkit/generate_templates.py --check

The source templates remain in modkit/examples. The desktop editor and CLI consume the
same generated bundle; they do not keep separate copies of the example scripts.
The Input observer template demonstrates independent P1/P2 buttons and analog controls
through `game.input.state` and finds each player's current family character through
`game.players.controlled`, with a native Options page and no gameplay changes.
Generated Lua completion includes typed players and snapshots. As with other projects, creation is disabled
until the creator chooses to test or enable it.

The UI smoke check uses QtWebEngine and an empty temporary install. It creates a mission,
edits source and metadata, validates, exports and imports it, checks keyboard dropdown
navigation, and captures desktop and narrow layouts without starting a game:

    python3 tools/bench/modkit_launcher_check.py --output /path/to/private-check

Pixel WebView, Android document providers, native Windows and game behavior still need
their own qualification. This check does not substitute for those runs. The
[full suite](PLAN.md) remains the release gate, including visual editors, typed assets,
world streaming and encounter integration. The save-system example is shelved; use the
small starter projects and the [language-pack workspace](TRANSLATIONS.md) first.

**Combat workshop** adds a commented encounter project through the same desktop
and Android source tools. It combines owned loaded brawlers, original health
operations, native death events, objectives, failure, retry and code reload.
See [combat authoring](COMBAT.md) for supported behavior and remaining campaign,
AI, collision and device qualification. Required named calls inside
`system.try_call` are included in project capabilities so older builds cannot
silently offer an incompatible template.

The [editor workspace guide](EDITOR_WORKFLOW.md) covers dock panels, the real game viewport, live assets, source shortcuts and offline help. Android imports/enables mod ZIPs; it does not include creator tools.
